name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,676

clue.text: Pound succeeded Dickensian character, female, past prime

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies
Uriah Heep, the scheming clerk in David Copperfield
F is the usual abbreviation for female
someone past their prime is getting on in years

explanation.surface: Ezra Pound is apparently followed by a Dickens figure, a woman no longer in her prime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like the poet or the currency, but it is the enclosure for animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A pound is an enclosure for animals, and a pen where sheep are kept is exactly that.

clue.text: Abandon vessel that may sink around Costa Rica

indicators.note: to go around something is to encircle it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: a submarine is a craft designed to submerge
CR is the international code for Costa Rica

explanation.surface: A sailor gives up on a leaky boat off the coast of Central America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel that may sink' sounds like a leaky ship, but it describes a craft built to dive.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrub a plan is informal for cancelling or dropping it, the same as abandoning it.

clue.text: Old stock about to come in for free

indicators.note: something that comes in enters another thing, so it sits inside it

blocks.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a stock phrase is a hackneyed, overused one
ca, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Old merchandise is about to arrive and be given away at no cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' looks like 'costing nothing', but it is a verb meaning to release.
explanation.definitionFit: To extricate someone is to release them from a difficulty or trap, which is to set them loose.

clue.text: Legal action going ahead

blocks.note: first meaning: a lawsuit or court case
second meaning: advancing, continuing onward

explanation.surface: A lawsuit is being allowed to continue.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase about a case being approved; it is two separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for a case brought in court and a participle meaning moving onward or continuing.

clue.text: Blade-wielder in leaving San Marino wounded

indicators.note: what leaves is no longer there, so those letters drop out
something wounded is damaged and knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters to remove
the small republic inside Italy, taken as written

explanation.surface: A swordsman is injured while departing from San Marino.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blade-wielder' suggests a swordsman; the blade is the flat end of an oar. Removing I and N from the country's name leaves SAMARNO to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A rower handles an oar, whose flat end is called the blade, so a rower wields a blade.

clue.text: Nocturnal creatures in sleeping quarters freeze

blocks.note: a dorm is a dormitory, a shared bedroom
to ice is to freeze or chill

explanation.surface: Night animals shiver in a cold dormitory.
explanation.walkthrough: The dormouse is famous for sleeping, which makes 'sleeping quarters' a neat fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormice are small rodents active at night and known for long hibernation, so they are night-active animals.

clue.text: Closely examine a little pink dress

indicators.note: a little of a word is just a small bit of it, here its opening letter

blocks.note: the first letter of the colour word
a robe is a long loose garment

explanation.surface: Someone inspects a dress that is slightly pink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A little pink' reads as a pale shade, but it means only a small part of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To probe is to investigate thoroughly, searching into something in detail.

clue.text: Preparation initially taken by sick?

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
to be ill is to be sick

explanation.surface: A medicine to be swallowed first thing by someone unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a medicine the ill take, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmaceutical preparation swallowed by a patient who is unwell is a tablet, the whole clue describing one.

clue.text: Piano used in old time musical work

indicators.note: something used in a thing is put inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
p is the musical marking for soft, piano
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A piano played in an old-fashioned piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: The piano letter goes between the two pieces for 'old time'.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a staged drama set to music, a large-scale composition for singers and orchestra.

clue.text: Bondsman to have letters dictated for comedian

indicators.note: what is dictated is spoken for someone to write down, so we go by sound

blocks.note: ERNIE is the machine that draws the UK's Premium Bond prizes
the plural of the letter Y is spoken like this

explanation.surface: A guarantor has a letter read out on behalf of a comic.
explanation.walkthrough: Premium Bonds are a British state savings lottery whose winning numbers are picked by a computer called ERNIE; 'letters' are the Ys, said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie Wise was the straight man of Morecambe and Wise, the much-loved British double act on television.

clue.text: Proportion shown as harangue avoids extremes

indicators.note: steering clear of the extremes means losing the two outermost letters

blocks.note: an oration is a long formal speech

explanation.surface: A measured, proportionate speech that steers clear of extreme views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Avoids extremes' sounds like moderate politics, but it trims the ends from the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio expresses the relative size of two quantities, which is what a proportion describes.

clue.text: Rustic retreat housing a clergyman

indicators.note: to house something is to give it room inside, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: rustic means of the countryside
a den is a private hideaway
taken as written

explanation.surface: A country cottage gives shelter to a vicar.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' does double duty in the surface but is just a letter inside the hideaway.
explanation.definitionFit: A rural dean is an Anglican priest overseeing a group of parishes, so he is a member of the clergy.

clue.text: Travels with old woman in express: one to hold up train?

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it, so these pieces go within another

blocks.note: to ride is to travel on a horse or vehicle
the old woman is a slang term for one's mother
to bid is to express, as in bidding farewell

explanation.surface: On an express service, someone travels with an older woman and wonders who will hold up the train.
explanation.walkthrough: The railway words throughout point to a rail robbery; the 'train' is the trailing part of a wedding dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridesmaids attend the bride at a wedding and may carry the long back section of her gown.

clue.text: Green plug first person in Paris should insulate

indicators.note: to insulate is to wrap round and enclose, so one piece covers another

blocks.note: je is French for I
a plug is a piece of publicity, an advert

explanation.surface: An electrician in Paris wraps a green plug for safety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plug' suggests electrics, which 'insulate' backs up, but it means a promotional mention.
explanation.definitionFit: Jade is a precious stone and also the name of its characteristic shade of green.

clue.text: Left field of substandard runners hitting this?

blocks.note: an idiom for eccentric or unconventional
a poor field of runners might bounce off a barrier, read literally

explanation.surface: A weak field of racers is left behind after crashing into an obstacle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left field' looks like part of a race report, but it is the American phrase meaning unconventional; the rest pictures runners rebounding from a barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: Something from left field is unexpected and strange, and the phrase here likewise means bizarre or unconventional.

clue.text: African golf club admits wife at noon

indicators.note: to admit someone is to let them inside, so one piece takes in another

blocks.note: the R and A, the Royal and Ancient Golf Club of St Andrews
W is the usual abbreviation for wife
N is short for noon

explanation.surface: A golf club lets a man's wife in at midday, and he is African.
explanation.walkthrough: The R and A in Scotland governs golf outside the US; 'golf club' looks like an iron or a clubhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rwandan is a native of Rwanda, a country in central-east Africa.

clue.text: Criminals who run insolvent businesses?

blocks.note: first meaning: people who knowingly handle stolen goods
second meaning: officials appointed to manage a bankrupt firm

explanation.surface: Crooks who operate failing companies.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests one set of shady operators; the question mark flags that the second sense is legitimate officials.
explanation.definitionFit: Receiving stolen goods is a crime, and an administrator appointed by a court over a failed company is also called this.

clue.text: Regular couple in Delft provide current address

indicators.note: a regular pair from a word means two letters taken at even spacing

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters of the Dutch town
to fend for oneself is to provide
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A Dutch couple in Delft supply their present home address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' looks like a street location, but it is a form of address, a title. 'Current' is electrical, not 'present'.
explanation.definitionFit: Effendi is a Turkish honorific title for a man of standing, used when speaking to him respectfully.

clue.text: Sunshine modified temperature in shelter

indicators.note: something modified has been changed, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: The weather warms as sunshine raises the temperature inside a shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Temperature' supplies its letter to the fodder rather than going inside anything.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nissen hut is a semicircular corrugated-iron building used for military accommodation and storage, a basic shelter.

clue.text: Bank invested in soccer tournament to make killing

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a cup is a knockout football competition
to bank is to tilt or lean, as an aircraft does

explanation.surface: A bank puts money into a football tournament to earn a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' and 'invested' paint finance, but bank is the verb to tilt.
explanation.definitionFit: To clean up and to make a killing are both idioms for earning a large profit quickly.

clue.text: Turned up to run clubs perhaps as hobby

indicators.note: turning something over flips it so it reads the other way round

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
clubs is one of the four suits in cards, hence 'perhaps'

explanation.surface: Someone showed up to manage golf clubs as a pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' reads as 'arrived', but the turning is applied to the word 'up' itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A pursuit is an activity one follows in leisure time, which is what a hobby is.

clue.text: Painter entertained by diplomat is Seurat

indicators.note: guests entertained by a host are held within the household, so the letters sit inside the phrase

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning these three words

explanation.surface: A diplomat plays host to an artist who claims to be Seurat.
explanation.walkthrough: Seurat is a painter too, a decoy pulling you toward a definition in the wrong place.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was a leading French artist, famous for bold colour and the Fauvist movement.

clue.text: Intend shortly to enclose grey brain part

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped
enclosing something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps round another

blocks.note: to mean is to intend
a grey day is a dull one

explanation.surface: Someone means soon to wrap up some grey matter of the brain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grey' with 'brain' suggests grey matter, but it means dreary. The shortened verb loses its N before wrapping round.
explanation.definitionFit: The medulla oblongata is the lowest section of the brainstem, controlling breathing and heart rate.

clue.text: Diamonds: diamonds get you murdered!

blocks.note: ice is slang for diamonds
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A gangster film warning: go after the jewels and you will be killed.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word is used twice, once as slang and once as the card-suit letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To ice someone is American slang for killing them, so iced is a crime-fiction word for murdered.

clue.text: River rising to claim female, small and delicate

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read from bottom to top, the other way round
to claim something is to take hold of it, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: the great river of Egypt
F is the usual abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A rising river sweeps away a slight young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The river is turned first, then takes in the letter for female.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin describes someone slight and dainty, like a fairy creature of folklore.

clue.text: Violin piece by leader strengthened position

blocks.note: the bridge is the part of a violin that holds the strings up
a head is a person in charge

explanation.surface: An orchestra's leader plays a piece on the violin, firming up their role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece' and 'leader' suggest music and the first violin of an orchestra, but they mean a component and a chief.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridgehead is a fortified foothold established in enemy territory from which an army can advance.

clue.text: Cuts links with space station

blocks.note: first meaning: reduces, as with pay or a tail
second meaning: a spacecraft joining up with an orbiting base

explanation.surface: Funding reductions sever ties with an orbiting station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuts links' reads as severing ties, but the clue splits after the first word into two separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: To dock wages is to reduce them, and a spacecraft docks when it couples with another vessel in orbit.

clue.text: Page taken from agreements in book before Romans

indicators.note: something taken from a thing is removed from it, so a letter disappears

blocks.note: P is the standard abbreviation for page
a pact is a treaty or agreement

explanation.surface: A page is removed from the agreements in a book about ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romans' suggests ancient history, but it is the Epistle to the Romans in the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: In the New Testament, the Acts of the Apostles immediately precedes Paul's Epistle to the Romans.

clue.text: Left cafe worried about university giving intended result

indicators.note: something worried is agitated and disturbed, so its letters are shaken up
about means surrounding, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: taken as written
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Someone left a cafe anxious about the university, and it had the desired effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a past-tense verb, but it is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Effectual means successful in producing a desired outcome, the same as achieving what was meant.

clue.text: A medic going round hospital for special case only

indicators.note: to go round something is to encircle it, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: taken as written
doc is short for doctor
H is the map symbol for hospital

explanation.surface: A doctor makes ward rounds in hospital, but only for one unusual patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going round hospital' suggests ward rounds; here the doctor's word wraps the hospital letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad hoc is Latin for 'for this', describing something arranged for one particular purpose only.

clue.text: End to regulations in American airspace

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
taken as written
US is short for American, of the United States

explanation.surface: Restrictions on flying in American skies are being lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Airspace' looks like aviation territory, but it is a literal air-filled space in the skull.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinuses are air-filled cavities in the bones of the face, so each is a space holding air.

clue.text: Driers that close when spinning

indicators.note: something spinning is whirled about, so its letters end up in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Tumble driers whose doors shut once the drum starts turning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driers' and 'spinning' suggest laundry machines, but the driers are cloths for washing-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea cloths are cloths used to wipe washed dishes dry, so they are things that dry.
